newsitem.title: HONG KONG: PRESS DIGEST-Hong Kong newspaper headlines-May 30.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-Hong Kong newspaper headlines-May 30.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Hong Kong press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- MING PAO -- Post-handover leader Tung Chee-hwa said the inner cabinet of the Special Administrative Region (SAR), as Hong Kong will be known after China takes back the territory on July 1, would make a decision on methods to form the first SAR legislature. It must be assured the future government was administrative-dominant, he added.
-- SING TAO - The share price of China-backed Beijing Enterprises shot to HK$40.20 in its trading debut on the Hong Kong stock exchange from the issue price of HK$12.48.

-- WEN WEI PO -- Chinese President Jiang Zemin said the principles laid down by late paramount leader Deng Xiaoping could not be changed and stressed that political reforms should be promoted and spiritual civilisation strengthened.
-- Tung said what Democratic Party leader Martin Lee had done was against the interests of Hong Kong people and that anybody who challenged the provisional legislature would fail.

-- ECONOMIC JOURNAL -- Chief Justice-designate Andrew Li said the SAR Court of Final Appeal would not start handling cases right after the handover because it had to wait for relative laws to be approved by the legislature. Li said he would go overseas to look for judges.

-- SOUTH CHINA MORNING POST -- Tung revealed his thoughts on the territory's future, with the development of industry a priority. His administration would actively consider calls for more imported labour and would seek to lure more multinational firms to the territory.

-- Market sources said a HK$1.9 billion share placement by mainland-backed China Everbright-IHD Pacific had collapsed after securities regulators said the company provided insufficient details about how the proceeds would be used.
-- HONGKONG STANDARD -- Cathay Pacific Airways' chairman said the carrier may seek compensation from Rolls-Royce over engine trouble that has grounded the airline's fleet of Airbus A330-300 planes.
